title: Forget 10,000 Steps—\x26#39;Japanese Walking\x26#39; Might Yield Even Better Health Benefits
titleZh: 试试这个在TikTok爆火的新走路方式
summary:
TikTok上，有不少用户表示这种健走方式有助于提升情绪、增强耐力、改善大脑健康等。一位创作者甚至声称，它比“每天走一万步”——这一长期被视为健康标准的做法——对身体更有益。但科学界对此怎么看？这种“日式健走”又该如何正确实施？以下是关于这一健走新趋势的关键信息。

来源：Health；作者：Cathy Cassata；原文发布时间：2025-06-20 20:10:00

paragraphs.contentEn: On TikTok, users say that the strategy can enhance mood, endurance, brain health, and more. One creator even claims that it’s better for you than simply walking 10,000 steps a day—long considered the quota for reaping health benefits. But what does science say—and how do you do Japanese walking properly? Here’s what to know about this trendy walking technique.
paragraphs.contentZh: TikTok上，有不少用户表示这种健走方式有助于提升情绪、增强耐力、改善大脑健康等。一位创作者甚至声称，它比“每天走一万步”——这一长期被视为健康标准的做法——对身体更有益。但科学界对此怎么看？这种“日式健走”又该如何正确实施？以下是关于这一健走新趋势的关键信息。

paragraphs.contentEn: What Is Japanese Walking? On social media, people often define Japanese walking as: Walking fast for three minutes; then, walking slowly for three minutes; repeating the pattern for five sets, reaching a total of 30 minutes. The method was first described in 2007 by researchers who tested it on a group of study participants in Japan.
paragraphs.contentZh: 什么是“日式健走”？在社交媒体上，人们通常将其定义为：先快步行走3分钟；随后慢走3分钟；重复以上模式进行5轮，总时长为30分钟。这一锻炼方法最早由研究人员于2007年提出，并在日本的一组受试者中进行了实验验证。

paragraphs.contentEn: The 2007 study found that, compared to people who walked at least 8,000 steps at a moderate pace daily for four or more days per week, those who participated in interval walking had greater improvements in strength, endurance and blood pressure levels. A more recent study from 2018 found that people who practiced interval walking for a decade showed a 20% improvement in leg strength and 40% improvement in peak exercise capacity. The researchers concluded that those participants had protected against age-associated declines in physical fitness. Even those who couldn’t maintain the workout for 10 years saw some partial improvements.
paragraphs.contentZh: 2007年的这项研究发现，与每周至少四天、每天以中等速度行走8000步的人相比，进行间歇式健走的人在力量、耐力和血压水平方面的改善更为显著。而发表于2008年的一项更近期的研究则发现，坚持间歇式健走长达10年的人，其腿部力量增强了20%，最大运动能力提高了40%。研究人员由此断定，这些参与者成功抵抗住了年龄增长带来的体能下降。即便未能坚持10年，参与者也普遍表现出一定程度的身体改善。

paragraphs.contentEn: Beyond those benefits, interval walking could potentially help you burn more calories and fat than walking at a steady pace—though it would depend on the intensity and frequency of your workout, Rekha B. Kumar, MD, an associate professor of medicine at Weill Cornell Medical College and Head of Medical Affairs at Found, told Health.
paragraphs.contentZh: 威尔康奈尔医学院医学副教授、Found公司医疗事务主管雷卡·B·库马尔医生在接受《健康》杂志采访时表示，除了上述这些健康益处，间歇式健走还有可能比匀速步行消耗更多的热量和脂肪——不过，这仍取决于锻炼的强度与频率。

paragraphs.contentEn: The bursts of faster-paced movement in interval walking can also help you meet the American Heart Association’s recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity per week. Interval walking is a good alternative for people who can’t run or do high-impact cardio, said Christina Brown, MS, CPT, a nutrition and weight loss coach.
paragraphs.contentZh: 间歇式健走中穿插的快步行走环节，也能帮你达到美国心脏协会所建议的“每周至少150分钟中等强度身体活动”的标准。营养与减重教练、营养学硕士兼注册私人教练克里斯蒂娜·布朗表示，对于无法进行跑步或高冲击有氧运动的人来说，间歇式健走是一个很好的替代方案。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Interval training—which can be done with pretty much any cardiovascular modality with a period of more intense training followed by a period of less intense—is really good for our cardiovascular and respiratory systems,” Brent Blaudow, a personal trainer and owner of Fitness Squared, told Health. When done consistently, he said, this training builds strength and endurance for those systems. Interval walking is "also great for people who feel that they are in a weight loss plateau as it changes up the intensity of their workout, which can help get them through the plateau,” Brown told Health.
paragraphs.contentZh: 私人教练、健身工作室Fitness Squared创始人布伦特·布劳多夫在接受《健康》杂志采访时表示：“间歇式训练——几乎适用于所有形式的有氧运动，其特点是在高强度与低强度之间交替进行——对心血管和呼吸系统都有显著益处。”他指出，长期坚持这种训练方式，有助于提升心肺系统的力量与耐力。布朗也告诉《健康》杂志，间歇式健走“对那些减重进入平台期的人同样非常有效，因为它调整了运动强度，有助于突破停滞”。

paragraphs.contentEn: How to Best Practice Japanese Walking? “To do interval training properly, there should be a clear delineation between the brisk and the slow,” Blaudow said. “Ideally, the walker should feel an increased heart rate towards the end of the brisk interval and feel at least a bit recovered by the end of the slow.” However, she recommends that people not used to exercise start with bouts of regular walking before working up to interval walking.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如何更好地进行“日式健走”？布劳多夫表示：“要规范地进行间歇式训练，快走与慢走之间应有明确的节奏区分。理想情况下，步行者在快走阶段结束时应感到心率上升，而在慢走阶段结束时应至少有所恢复。”不过她也提醒，对于没有运动习惯的人，可以从常规步行开始，待身体逐步适应后，再过渡到间歇式健走训练。

paragraphs.contentEn: “People with uncontrolled blood pressure, severe arthritis, balance disorders, or those recovering from cardiac events should check with their doctor before starting interval walking,” Brown said. If walking briskly has been part of your exercise routine, Blaudow said you may not need three minutes of slower walking. “If you already use intervals in your cardio training, I think you should make them more challenging,” he said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 布朗提醒：“血压控制不佳、患有严重关节炎、存在平衡障碍，或正从心脏病发作中恢复的人，在开始间歇式健走前一定要先咨询医生。”布劳多夫则指出，如果本身的锻炼中已有快走等环节，可能不需要安排长达三分钟的慢走恢复时间。他补充说：“如果你已经在进行有氧间歇训练，不妨考虑进一步提高训练强度。”

paragraphs.contentEn: While it’s possible that Japanese walking may offer more benefits than walking at a regular pace, getting more walking in—of any type—can have positive health effects. One study found that getting as little as 4,000 steps daily may be enough to lower a person’s risk of early death. Aside from the health benefits, walking is simply convenient, Brown pointed out. You don’t need anything besides a pair of sneakers. “Setting a daily step goal regardless of whether you are walking at a steady state or doing interval walking is a wonderful way of keeping the body active and moving,” she said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 相比匀速步行，尽管日式健走或许能带来更多益处，但无论采用哪种方式，增加日常步行本身就对健康有积极影响。有研究显示，每天哪怕只走4000步，也可能足以降低早逝风险。布朗指出，步行不仅有益健康，本身也极为便利，你所需要的，仅仅是一双运动鞋。她总结道：“无论是匀速步行还是间歇健走，设定一个每天的步数目标，都是保持身体活力和运动状态的好方法。”

expressions.expression: While it is possible that …… may offer more benefits than ……, getting more …… can have positive …… effects.
expressions.meaning: 尽管……可能比……带来更多益处，但增加……仍然会对……产生积极影响。
expressions.example: While it is possible that reading literature may offer more benefits than watching movies, getting more exposure to stories in any form can have positive effects on empathy.
